Content:
Absolutely love these. I originally bought the 72ct. After a couple months I decided I liked them well enough to buy the 130ct. For a larger variety.
(First pic is of the 2 sets side by side without the opposite sides of the fold out sections.)

There’s a couple differences between the 2 sets outside of the obvious color range. The 72ct came with just the markers in the case. I expected the same from the 130ct however I was pleasantly surprised to find a baggy of replacement nibs and instructions on how to replace said nibs as well as instructions on how to fix them if they become dried out.

Pros:
- Easy control
- Smooth consistency and flow.
- Juicy
- Bright, bold, vibrant, gorgeous colors.
- If your main qualifier is brush tips these are perfect! Capable of creating thick lines but also capable of creating those fine details as well as get into the smaller nooks and crannies.
- layer well with like colors.
- No smudging or smearing.
- Dry quickly
- Fine tip is great for dotting. I’ve used them primarily for adding dots and other embellishments over top blocks of color.
- Case is well made and makes for easy storage as well as taking them on the go.
- good color variety in both sets making smooth and subtle color transitions a breeze.
- NO BLEEDING

Cons:
- 3 of the markers in the 72ct arrived dry, however not entirely. (Upon receiving instructions in the larger set in how to fix this I feel this has been made up, tho these instructions should be included in the smaller sets.)
- The fine point is not very fine, it is indeed a small bullet tip that doesn’t do well at all for fine details. The brush tip works better.
- There is some color consistency issues between the brush and bullet tip on some colors however slight.
- Some of the fine tips leave behind fibers.
- These do NOT work well on fabrics, colors will not show.
- Majority of the colors do not appear well on black surfaces. (This does not seem to be the case coloring over lines in coloring books).
- Not all colors layer nicely as these are water based, if you attempt to layer colors on opposite sides of the spectrum they just mix.
- There is only one Red in the 72ct.
- Some colors are more transparent than opaque in the fine tip.

Overall, very worth it. I have sets Ive paid more for that were far less quality.

Content: Now THIS is a set of acrylic pens! Every set has strengths and weaknesses, so I'm always on the lookout for certain things in particular:- Caps that can be retained on the end of the markers- A set of colors which all have good contrast against one another- Brush tips, so I can do both very fine and very broad strokes with one tip- A good array of DARK colors, not just a good array of midtones and light colors- A good box or case that shows every marker at once and doesn't require lots of searching for an empty spot to put a marker back intoThis set has four of the five things. There aren't many dark colors in here. But I can say that this set has enough color & saturation values for you to be able to make an amazing range of stuff. You can paint things that require lots of fine variations - fancy birds, iridescent bugs, opal, space pictures, and more! There are also a LOT of skin tone options so you can make an accurate likeness of just about anyone. Lots of tan-/dun- like colors for realistic animal fur too. Finally, there are a lot of distinct hues in the red, purple, and pink parts of the spectrum - something I don't see in other marker sets. It's a really good palette.The brush tips are a joy to use and the paint feels consistent. Even the reds and yellows go on very strong, and I don't have to go back over them a lot like I do with other paint pens. In the picture, you can see some doodles I made on a dark rock, and I only had to draw each thing one time to get colors that solid. It's definitely good paint with a lot of pigment in it. I really like the range of color and saturation values on offer because I can use a ton of colors without making something that clashes or hurts my eyes.If you're gonna use or move the box often, I recommend cutting some small holes in the top of the lid. This breaks the vacuum so the lid comes off much more easily.I recommend the pens!

Content:
Tried 3 different sets, these 30 single brush tips and 2 sets of 48 of the dual tipped markers, one from this brand and the other from Pagather that were all in similar price rance during sales. The main question was to see how the brands differed, but also to understand why the dual tip set from THIS brand was so much cheaper despite the additional tip and carry case that these lack. Well, the Dual tip is not worth it, imo. I felt the difference in the weight of the pens, which clearly is due to the amount of LIQUID in them, and these win by a mile. I can see the duals running dry in much less time.

Given the value of how much more coverage you will get from these, this is worth the money where the other is not so much. I easily would choose this set of brush tips only over the dual marker, if only because fine lines are just as achievable with this tip anyway. The fine point of the other is more like a marker than a brush, which maybe is preferable for those without as much motor control in the hands, like kids. But for the price to usage ratio, I think there is much more to found in these.

I am currently considering how much color variety I really need, and whether I am willing to return all three sets to get the 48 single tip markers and case to go with it, or maybe just go with 36 since neither of those is discounted and I don't really NEED this, just thought it might be nice go have as a crafty sort of person who loves art supplies. If I were wanting them for creating paintings myself, I would definitely get the 48 set of these over any of the dual tipped varieties.

If I had these in a zippered case, I wouldn't even think twice about the extra colors and be very satisfied. These seem to be vibrant, more like opaque paint than watercolor, and supposedly waterproof, and seem to have the most favorable reviews with fewer complaints than other brands.

So the only question is how much more is that case worth to me if I decide to return these or not.

Content: I am actually really impressed by these markers. The ink flows really smoothly into the nib, which feels really smooth to paint and write with. While you have to give the pens a good shake to get the ink mixed up initially and after sitting a while, that’s it. No annoying press down with a bare nib until the ink flows the first time, just shake, uncap and go.The colors are also surprisingly opaque. You can actually layer lighter colors right on top of the darker colors without much of an issue at all. The white did sometimes take a layer or two, but most of the other lighter color just went on as easily as if they had a white background.The only issue I ran into is that blending the colors doesn’t really work. You can a little if you go back and forth while the ink is wet, but not very well. This is alright with some of the colors that have a variety, because you can just go along the different markers and make a gradient that way. However, where I found I needed a few shades was brown, and things didn’t work out super well with that. That’s relatively common in paint pens though, so it is what it is. Overall, I think these paint pens work really well, and I will be using mine a lot.

Content: I was very hopefully that this would be the right one. I wasn't sure what to get as this is my first try at glitter on fabric. Making a quilt for a little girl. Decided to go with unicorns and I thought it would be nice to add glitter that is made for fabric.It does go on fabric, and it does have glitter. But . . . There is the in-between; and that is where my disappointment is from. I know I should have known better, thought out all the aspects --- but it is now Oh Crap!!Did my routine of placing the material, the carbon paper (that is supposed to disappear when iron is used but didn't) place the coloring page of what I want to trace, this one, unicorn. After tracing I pick the colors I need for what I am making. I hand paint my quilts; I'm like a kid with all kinds of markers and can paint what I want LOL.OK, serious now. Have my fabric with the outline of my unicorn, this one will be pink.Using my acrylic paint markers I paint in the colors. For the glitter, that will go on the mane, tail and hooves.Here is the OH Crap! ! ! I had shaken the tube before I took the cap off, push down so the glitter paint can soak into the point. But, when it slowed down and no more glitter I figured just shake it. So, I shook it, and glitter landed on the fabric, my top, work table and a Whole of Mess!It may not be fair to blame the company, and I don't totally blame them. But (don't you just love those buts lol) to me they failed in not noting in larger font, darker color, or even a NOTICE warning. If a child had done this and gotten into her eyes, an elderly lady has glasses on, and the glitter paint landed on them? Not a happy ending.Maybe I should have gotten a magnifying glass and looked at every word. I stupidly trusted a business to state: Notice -- have cap on before shaking --- in large enough letters for a 69-year-old woman, with very poor eyesight so she doesn't make such a mess.And I know that, if I am honest, that I am as much to blame as they are. But (yep, another one again) I still have a low opinion of the product, having to constantly shake it, pushing the tip down to get the paint to flow and make sure glitter comes out, and tapping the bottom to get the glitter to spread instead blocking the opening. Sigh!

Content:
I’m impressed with the quality and variety of these acrylic markers! They’re the kind you have to prime by shaking and pressing down the nib a few times but they prime much more easily than some so I didn’t find that to be a hindrance.

The tips are definitely fine enough to use for line work, lettering or small details and the ink flows very smoothly.

The only thing I haven’t had a chance to test so far is how long the markers will last. But with that in mind, they are easy to use and the color goes on super sheer. Between that and the fact that this is the best color selection I’ve found in an acrylic marker set so far, they are definitely worth purchasing.

The price of $52.99 is a bit higher than I’d usually pay (although it’s not a bad deal considering that it’s still less than 50 cents per marker) but the seller is currently offering a 50% off coupon. At that price, this marker set is an absolute steal.

Content:
These paint pens are simply fabulous! Not a marker or a pen, but actually paint in a pen. So much fun to play around with! I had just sketched out a little scene from Pinterest, trying to decide if I wanted to purchase the stamp set. Since it was just sitting there I decided to use these paint pens … FYI, I had a blast and was pleasantly surprised.

First you have to prime each pen to get the paint flowing. Originally I had used a permanent ink sketching pen to do this and I was pretty amazed that these paint pens are opaque and could completely cover my black sketching ink. I purposely left some of the black in showing, but I could have covered it if I had wanted too.

I discovered a fun little hack. On the paper towels I was using to prime these pens, I also had a piece of clear scotch tape. I primed some ink on the tape and it stayed wet long enough to dip a wet paintbrush in the ink and smear it onto the watercolor paper that my sketch was on. An improvised paint pallet! I had to move quickly, but it was doable.

When you prime these paint pens, use multiple layers of paper towel as the ink is permanent and you dont want to mark up your work surface. I got these to use on wooden Christmas ornaments with my grandkids so we will all be wearing painting aprons to protect our clothes.

I found this set to be so much fun to use. Just remember that this really is paint flowing out of a pen. It dries quickly. The metallics are especially sparkly. Any artsy kid or adult would love this set!

Content: UPDATE::: Y'all I love these markers so muchI've been using them consistently since I got them in october- no issues with drying AT ALL, though I would recommend taking them out and giving them a good shake periodically as a precaution.I find that they work smoother/more painterly on canvas or primed surfaces- they dry a bit too quickly on paper and soak up a bit more, but they still didn't even bleed through my mixed media sketchbook, so that's a major win!The case does take up a lot of space when you have all the sections out and accessible, which isn't my favorite, but is only a minor hindrance. No issues with snapping or breaking at all.I still have nitpicks about the color range (lack of oranges and yellows, mostly) but have found that, while they're still wet, they do mix quite nicely. You can achieve a lot of good in-between colors by mixing on the surface you're creating on before the marks dry.Though I am still so sure I will run out of white and yellow before anything else, which has me wishing I could buy individuals.Despite that, these are one of my favorite sets of art supplies in recent years. I'm obsessed.Updated pros/consPROS:-Surprisingly opaque-very saturated colors-dries fast and layers well (colors do dry a bit darker, as it goes with acrylic)-The brush tip is actually the best, no more pumping a paint markerCONS:-color range is lacking a bit in oranges, yellows, and dark colors-case takes up a lot of space when opened--------------------------------original review--------------------------------(I got these today, so this is a 'first impressions' review)I'm a artist and art instructor by trade, and I like to use a wide variety of materials to make recommendations to students as well as find new supplies for myself.These markers are pretty solid- I like acrylic paint for its opaque layering properties, as well as the quick dry, and these markers are pretty effective at both. As with acrylic paint, you do have some transparency and a need to layer, especially on lighter colors like white and yellow, or on top of darker colors. But overall, the coverage is pretty solid and the saturation is impressive.The case is a bit weird, you have to be careful separating the layers (they tuck into these little ridges at the back to hold together, and I can see there being a risk of snapping) but otherwise it seems convenient.The color range is odd. Acrylic dries darker than it applies, so after you let them sit for a moment you do have deeper hues, but the black included is SO much darker than the deepest of any other color.I'd really love to see a deep jewel tone range for each hue so I can achieve solid depth without just resorting to black. A deep alizarin crimson, phthalo blue or Paynes grey, deep viridian- the problem, I assume, is that these markers all have an almost chalky binder to keep the opacity up, and it sacrifices the deeper values as a result (many of the above listed colors are traditionally transparent.) So I'm not sure this would even be possible with the current pigment/binders used.Still, it would be wonderful to have a really deep set of colors, and if I'm just missing them in this 60 pack, I'd love to be directed to where I can grab them.Also, there's not a lot of orange options, and there are a whole lot of certain other colors, like green and pink.Anyway tldr;PROS:-nice opacity-very Saturated-dries fast and layers well-smooth flow with convenient brush tipCONS:-color range is lacking in oranges, yellows, and dark colors-case is a bit confusingI'll come back after a couple months of use to update on whether the markers have any trouble or not, but as of today I'm liking them.

Content: These were really nice paint pens. The things that kept me from giving it five stars were as follows: the case is kind of a pain to deal with. You have to unsnap each layer and lay them all out to have easy access to any color. And then when putting the cases back together you have to make sure that the clip on the case above doesn’t get snapped in when you clip the one below. It just seems very unnecessary when a zipper case that you can unfold and lay out works much better. I have another set of 60 of these almost identical pens and they came in a zipper case that was much easier to deal with. I will say that the case looks very nice tho. My second problem that I took a star off for is that some caps fit nicely in the back of the pen when using it while others were too loose and wouldn’t stay on. I don’t like having loose lids to keep track of and it just seems strange that some would do that while others didn’t.As far as the actual marker goes tho, I would say that they perform at a five star quality. On the swatch sheets I only did one layer for each shade except for the white on the black sheet. I did two layers on that trying to see how many I would need to get a good solid coverage on black. I would say three layers would do it. I don’t ever color on black paper so it’s not an issue to me but that might be a problem covering black lines in coloring books. Rarely would I want to cover a line with white so again that’s fine with me. I also absolutely love the color selection! There are a great range of colors and many neutrals which I appreciate. On white paper it only took one layer for opacity. In fact if you look at the sample flower I painted the darker blue/green outline around the flower had red below it. I changed my mind after coloring it red And then went over with the darker shade of blue/green and it only took one coat to cover the red. I was impressed by that.The presentation of the set was really sharp too! It came with a thick black envelope containing all the swatch sheets, instructions, and sample coloring sheets. Shuttle Art if you’re reading this please make a coloring book specifically using that same white paper and gray outlines for acrylic markers! I would buy that in a heartbeat! I love that paper! Also the case looks really nice setting on your shelf. While I’m not crazy about its functionality it does look sharp and is nice quality. For these reasons I think this set would be a perfect gift for the color lover in your life. It feels a step above the others. Just fantastic presentation.Update: after playing with these for awhile and getting the new pastel set I decided to change the rating to a 5*. The case has NOT been the pain that I thought it would be and for the value of the pens it’s worth it. I would highly recommend these to anyone! Btw if you have the set of 60 and get the pastel set too, the trays DO fit together into one stack. They are a pleasure to color/paint with. 🥰

Content: I use pens like these all the time in painting my 3D resin prints. They're great for experimenting 'cause you can try out different colors and color combinations on your prints without having to clean your brushes out each time. You can blend colors together easily on your prints and you can get rid of mistakes just by wiping the paint off. Then, once you get the color scheme you like laid out, you can continue using these pens to apply your final paint job or you can transition to brushes and just use what you just did as a guide.These also work well when it comes to actual painting. You can paint straight areas like pipes and panels and walls with no problem. If you use metallic colors, you can make these things look nice and real. If you can't reach into some areas 'cause the tips are too wide,  you can then just use a qtip or traditional brush to push the paint into those areas and spread it around.The black pens come in real handy for weathering and fake shadows. You can selectively paint over some areas to apply that paint and then just wipe those areas off to leave paint only in the recesses to simulate weathering or shadows. These work great for that.Just be aware that there are limitations with using paint pens like this. You can't easily paint large areas 'cause you'll end up leaving visible pen strokes. You can get around this issue to a certain extent just by gently wiping your painted areas down and applying perhaps more coats. But still large areas could prove difficult.

This is a great set and I started playing with it the day it arrived. The paint markers come in a sturdy case that snaps shut. It's nice that you can see all the markers at the same time. It's a bit tough popping them out, but they stay in place. The lids also securely snap shut but you really have to be sure they are shut -- look at the cap to be sure it's all the way down because it takes some pressure to close them. Because of this, the lids won't fall off.

It comes with a color card so you can test each color and know what they look like, but the layout is confusing and doesn't follow the order of the pens in the case. Why not make them go in the same order? It's very weird but I got most of the colors on it. Still can't find one but eventually I will. The problem is that the paint color is on the top of the cap, so it's hard to see them when the markers are in the case. Also, some are printed in white on light colors so they are really hard to read because they are also very small.  It would be much easier if they were printed on the sides of the pens so you could see them all at once. There is a system to naming them, such as BV1 for blue violet 1. Some of them don't make sense, but most are easy to figure out. Again, all the colors in white on the sides would be a great improvement in the future.

The paint is very nice -- it's really opaque, goes on smooth, and is a bit wetter than typical paint markers like this so you have a bit of time to blend it. Not much, but enough for small areas. You don't have to pump these to prime them as they are ready to go. The tip has a nice flexible point that makes both thin and thick marks really well.

The color selection is what really makes me happy -- this set has not one but two actual REDS! Holy cow, I have been waiting to find a set with red and not some coral/vermillion color pretending to be red. There is a bright red and dark red and they look beautiful. The paint dries darker so don't be fooled by the color you initially see. I was worried the darkest purple wasn't really dark, but it dried to a beautiful dark violet color. The dark brown also dried to a nice deep brown -- another color that is hard to find. I do wish the darkest blue and green were darker, but they're still nice. The green include a light lime green as well as regular grass green, cool greens, olives, and some blue-greens. There is a nice array of purples with warm and cool tones. The pinks are okay -- the dark one is darker than most others I've tried, but still not a true magenta. There is a nice selection of light pinks. The yellows and oranges are wonderful, with shades all the way from light yellow to dark orange and even includes mustard. There are a lot of colors that I would classify as pale skin tones, as well as an array of light to darker browns. There are far more light colors than dark, so this is great if you need pastels. The black is nice and dark with no noticeable cool or warm tones. Overall, I am really happy with the color selection; the cap colors come close to what you actually get.

This set is a bit more expensive than others, but you get so many colors that the cheaper sets just don't have. And the paint is better quality. If you like painting with paint markers, you will love this set.

Content:
I have been collecting a few sets of acrylic marker/paint pents so that I could do some detail work on paintings, models, or artwork and not have to use a brush for some things.

HOW THIS COMES
This comes in a great case. It has a lot of room in it and is very well laid out. They are easy to see and use from a chair or table.

MARKERS
The markers themselves are brush on one end and fine point on the other. There is no window on the side to see the paint level and you do not have to shake them to get them to work.

COLORS
This set has a LOT of colors. If you do anything like rock painting or other bright colored projects, you will have plenty to choose from. Some of the colors are similar, but I don't mind because if one runs out or dries up, I can just change to another.

PERFORMANCE
On paper, these are pretty good intensity. They are not as opaque or thick as some others I have but they still work great for projects that don't need a heavy opaque laydown of paint. On canvas, they are hit and miss. Some of the colors are more transparent than others and will need more coats. The best ones on canvas are the metallics as they cover well and the texture is excellent. I have included a quick photo I took of some tests I ran showing the metallics up close. I hope you can see it.

DRY TIME
These dry very quickly. On paper it is really fast. On canvas, it takes a little bit of time, but not much before you can put on another layer.

USE
You will need to use these. Once you get them, use them. They will most likely dry out pretty quickly and you won't get to have fun with them if you wait too long. This is the type of art tool you want to enjoy when you get it and not put it away for that project you will probably not get to anyway.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For models, artwork, and even rock paintings, these are decent acrylic marker pens. The paints are somewhat transparent in some colors, so plan accordingly

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. For what these are, they are really nice. I love the case and apprecaite how easy it is to see them, store them, and take them with me when I want to do a project. I can do it in a chair or at a table. I just have to remember to push to use them before they dry up at some point so I can enjoy them while they are still working.

Content: Glitter Paint Pens16 Pens0.7 mmFine TipThis is a nice set of paint pens, but I think they are a little misleading. While the paint does have glitter in it, they are actually metallic. You can see the glitter shine, but these are definitely metallic. All of the colors are vibrant, saturated in color, and true to the pen caps color. I find that one pass of coloring in an area is enough but two really makes it pop. Allowing dying time between layers keeps even notebook paper smooth. Before use the pens need to be started. It does have directions on the back of the package though. All you have to do is shake each pen well. Then on scrap paper or cardboard push the tips of the pens down about 7-10 times. It pumps the paint into the tip. I always make color charts for all of my pens and markers so that I can accurately see the colors. The first swatching of colors was a bit heavy, paint wise. But that's because the pens were new. After that and letting them sit for a while (maybe an hour) they were perfect for fine line writing or drawing. If you pump the tip more the paint comes out heavy again. That can be good for filling in larger spaces. Overall, I do really like these paint markers. I would like to give them 5 stars. I have to take one star off because they are metallic glitter pens. Not glitter alone pens. Oh, and there is no smell at all.

Content: I purchased this item because I am an artist and I've become very comfortable with the Ohuhu brand name. I saw that they had this new acrylic marker out and I wanted to try it out.My opinion is that this is sort of a niche acrylic marker, because the tips are a little different than what I'm used to. Compared to other brands on the acrylic marker market these brush tips seem to be sort of hairy, and seem to shred at the tip ever so slightly.The results are different. It isn't like an alcohol felt tip that produces the same fine lines and bold edges until the tip starts to degrade. It is sort of like a brush tip of an actual paint brush tip. What I've achieved with this tip is either very fine sketchy lines or blocked in areas of color.What I mean about sketchy lines is that the brush seems to be designed to feel like a paint brush. If you lightly drag the brush across the page you're going to get thin lines, but they aren't going to be consistent. What you get is a thin sketchy line that is fine, but sort of annoying at the same time. I did play with them for a while and after a while I figured out how to use that sketching motion to get some fine points and light lines, but still the ability to paint a long consistent thin line just doesn't really happen or apply here.What happens is if you put the slightest amount of pressure on the tip, you're not really going to get a fine line anymore. The flow of this pen is really good and the paint sort of pools. What you get a thicker line that is very satisfying, and consistent. What I'm used to is a pen that can produce thick and thin lines in the same stroke. With this pen I find myself laying down thick lines, then going back over them and refining the lines to look like it was a thick and thin stroke.My opinion is that it is a good marker. I love the thin body style, and the paint flow is remarkably premium. I love that the set comes in such a nice organizational travel/ storage case and as always Ohuhu's Colors just seem to be so dramatic and satisfying. Actually, I think that is what I like best about this pen. The colors are vivid and beautiful. Compared to other acrylic markers, Ohuhu's colors just seem to pop more, are more precise and opaque on the first coat.On the note of how I feel about the tips?I think I've settled with this marker, I can say that I suggest them but I will also say just be ready for a little bit of a curve ball if you're used to another brand. The brush tips are just slightly different than competitors and maybe you will like them. My conclusion on the tips is that they are niche and have function, I consider it to be a tool whereas because it is different it is valuable. This marker can and does become usable for certain detail situations.Overall, I will say this is a good pen. I think that most people are going to be satisfied with them. I've been a little nit picky about the tips, but I am an artist and things like this that appear to me will probably appear to other artists, so as a reviewer I want to make note of them.Great marker and highly suggested.

Content: This 24-piece acrylic paint pen kit is a blast--and at a little over $1 a pen, it gives you a lot of entertainment hours for your buck!The set comes in a beautifully decorated hardcover case, with the name "Ohuhu" (leaf in the 'O'), and drawings of leaves, flowers, stars, cactus, a cute gecko, peaceful dove, and other geometrics, designed to inspire, printed on the front in white. The back has Ohuhu's motto, "Draw. Feel. Empower." and a bunch of legal data printed on it. The zipper on the case moves very smoothly, and each pen has its own velcro loop to hold it secure in travel. This would make a perfect Plein Air sketch set, so light and easy to use.Inside, there is a multilingual instruction booklet and 3 swatch cards. 1 swatch card is filled out and has a white background, and there are also two blanks: one white and one black. I encourage you to fill both of these out, first, to prime your pens and get them ready to do an art, and second, so you can notice how the different background colors affect the perceived color of the pens. Even though you are using the exact same color on both cards, the final outcome looks VERY different. After that, you're ready to go!The colors of the paint are opaque, provided you let the bottom colors dry before adding more on top. This takes maybe a minute. You can also blend the colors just a bit by working two colors together quickly, but be careful that you don't foul and muddy your pen tips.Protip: if you've treated your item with gesso (highly recommended), you can blend, work, and even dilute the colors with a damp brush and a little water, allowing you to create watercolor-like effects or blend and smooth sharp lines. The gesso protects your item from the water and smooths the surface in order to accept the paint more readily. It's fairly cheap and available here on Amazon. Think of it as primer, except for art!These pens may not be as versatile as a full acrylic paint set, but neither are they as expensive or as messy. For a more advanced artist, these pens make a great color sketch set so you can get ideas down in the books quickly and conveniently, then you can use your full acrylic or oil paint set to make a full final copy. These paints are great for casual artists or smaller multimedia art projects such as rock painting or just adding a few quick touches to a knitting or sewing project. Not everybody wants or needs to bother with a full paint kit. These pens are also great for card-making and stencils. I'm sure there's a ton of other uses I've forgotten, or don't have the wit to imagine. 10/10, versatile, affordable, and FUN.

Content:
"30 Colors Waterproof Dual Tip Acrylic Paint Pens, Dot & Fine Tip" is a set of 30 markers with a dot tip on one side and a fine tip on the other. Unlike regular markers, these are filled with acrylic paint.

-------------
Pros:
* Using acrylic markers is faster and easier than using paint brushes.

* They don't need to be shaken and primed before use. You can just open the container and get started! (Unlike most markers that are filled with a substance that's thicker than ink.)

* The quality of the tips is adequate for multiple surfaces.

* The dot tip is surprisingly handy if you have trouble making perfect circles by hand, like most people do. XD

* The paint flows easily, so the markers move smoothly. That specifically makes them good for painting, writing, and detail work.

* The acrylic "ink" is easily layered, doesn't bleed (even on paper), and works well on multiple surfaces, which makes it a fantastic tool for craft projects.

* The acrylic is water-based, which makes it washable, so clean up is a breeze!

* The paint dries quickly.

* The pens -don't- dry out quickly.

* There's no strong smell.

-------------
Meh:
* The markers come in a range of pastel and medium colors with only a few dark and metallic colors. If that's what you're looking for, you're golden. If not, you won't buy these anyway, so it doesn't matter. :)

* The marker colors are named AND numbered, making finding replacements quick and easy. However, this is only true on the back of the box, NOT on the pens themselves, so you'll need to keep the list on the box / take a picture of it / whatever if you want that information.

* They suffer the same issues as using acrylic paints... because they ARE acrylic paints.

For example, the markers work on smooth surfaces like glass and plastic, but when you try to paint over a part that you've already painted, there's a chance that it will remove the paint on these surfaces instead of adding more (Sharpies and dry erase markers do this, too). And sometimes the lighter colors will be a little see-through, and might take multiple coats to fully cover a surface.

These are very common paint issues, but people sometimes seem to forget that acrylic markers are paint, not traditional markers, and as such, they act like paint. XD

-------------
Cons:
* None! At least, not yet. :)

-------------
With the quality, versatility, and variety of these paint markers, $30 for 80 markers ($0.38 each) is an absolute STEAL, even considering that you're getting less paint with each marker than is standard.

And even with taking the lack of replacement options into account, if given the choice, I would choose to order these again. The color variety is just too good to pass up. :)

I hope that this helps! :D

Content:
I am NOT an artist - I am a crafter and, therefore, my review is based on how I would use these paint markers. There’s a lot to like:
- There’s a nice variety of colors though some of are subtle variations
- The bullet (or dot) end is a nice bullet point, which will be good for mandala painting (for me, on river rocks)
- You can get a pretty fine line with the fine tip
- You don’t have to do a lot prep just to get started (e.g., pressing down nibs, waiting for paint to appear, etc.); simply uncap and go to town
- The caps click when closing so you know it’s firmly capped (some other markers have dried on me when I inadvertently did not put on the caps tight enough)
- While it’s waterproof on surfaces, it washes off clean from your hands.
- Good price point.

So why not 5 stars? Well…these might be minor to some, but for me, I was kind of “meh”:
- The colors are in no way labeled. Yes, you can see the color from the cap BUT, as I mentioned, a couple colors are very similar. I swatched all but one pen, but because there’s no number or name, I can’t figure out which one I missed.
- I do like a solid, clicking cap. However, there was an inconsistency - some caps were fine and easy to open; a few were on so tightly, it was a struggle to open. By the time I got one or two uncapped, I was grumpy.
- The coverage is okay, not super-duper. To get a good opaque coverage, you have to wait for one layer of color to dry then go over it. Not a big deal, but the white could be whiter. The silver and gold are nice but my other acrylic metallic markers are more shimmery/shiny. Again, not a bit deal.

Overall, for the number of pens, the quality of the color, and the price point, this is a good purchase - at least from a crafter’s perspective.

Content:
These markers work well. Like a paint pen, you have to push on the tip to get the ink to flow down into the tip (but the first time, you can see the flow, so it's easy to judge when the tip is ready)
NOTE: The ink in these pens are very liquid -- they take a minute to dry once on the paper, so if you touch it too soon, it will smear!
The lines made will vary in width based on how hard and how slow/fast you press when laying down the ink (again, very much like a paint pen). You can't get super-fine lines, but thicker lines are easy enough to master. (and, if you press too hard, you'll get a blob!)
The end result is not so much a "glitter" look (like you get when crafting and laying down a thin line of glue then sprinkling glitter on top of it), but rather a "shine with a sparkle" kind of look. If you look straight on, there's a bit of shimmer, but at an angle, the glitter look is more noticeable. (Thanks to reviewer Angelica for her video -- it shows perfectly exactly what I am talking about!).
My wife is the "crafter" in our household, and she says these are exactly what she was hoping for -- give them 5 stars!

Content:
I spent many years as a professional graphic, commercial and fine artist, mostly graphic. So my opinion may not really fit with the average person who would use these paints. I think the average person who will buy acrylic paints will like them, because they are used to using acrylics, and are not as picky as I am about precise colors. the paint is acrylic, so it does what acrylic paint does. The best thing about them is The tips. They are amazing. They are not a felt tip, they are a brush tip, so you can make a tiny line by touching very lightly, or wider depending on the pressure you put on the tips, all the way to a really wide line by laying it a little sideways. no need to have double tip, and as far as I can tell, they do not moosh down and loose their sharp point. I have not used them a lot, so I don't know how long they last. The paint dries very quickly, so it will be important to click the lids fully on, each time you quit using one, even for a few minutes.

The reasons I gave this a 3 star rating is that  a) at least one of the most standard colors I would use a lot, and is critical for painting plants or flowers is not included. There is a good light green, but no dark green, and the middle green, is not a good standard green. In my opinion it is a little too blue to look right on green leaves. Unfortunately, you cannot blend acrylics, so you cannot create your own colors, which is why acrylics are not my favorite type of paint. b) these are more expensive than most of the other acrylic paint sets I saw on Amazon, so I don't think it is a good value (one set has 72 colors for about the same price.)

Honestly I can't think of any negatives to mention. These are high quality paint markers that work well and look great. The price point is excellent compared to premium brands with the product itself performing just as well. Highly recommend to

Content:
As long as you shake these paint markers before using, they work great. I love that you can layer light colors over dark ones. I am extremely sensitive to chemicals, and these have nothing in them that triggers my allergies.

They have two tips, a blunt one for wide strokes and a pointy one for variable line width. I personally could not control the line width of the pointy tip, but I imagine that someone with good fine motor control could. So it's not really great for super detail work, because if you accidentally press a little too hard, the pen will create a wide stroke instead of thin.

There are just a couple of minor things I think could have been designed better. To tell which tip is which without removing the caps, you need to read the fine print on the middle section of the pen. It would have been nice if they made the caps different to make it more obvious. Also, the box doesn't work great for storage. You have to dig around to get the pens out, and they don't always go back in easily.

These detractions are minor. Overall, the pens are a joy to use.

Content: I ordered this paint pen set for the wide assortment of colors. I have other sets, but their colors are limited, especially with the pinks and greens. This set has an excellent selection and even some metallic colors, too. The pens are comfortable to hold and use. I prefer the round barrel than the square shape with rounded edges (like my other sets). I have more control with this set. Even though they don't have to be prepped before use, when you first use them, the paint is a bit lighter and gets a richer hue as you make more strokes. The coverage is pretty good, but you may need to go over your area more than once to get full coverage. I tried them on an unpainted vinyl doll head and a foam clay flower, and both pieces received the paint very well, but I did have to keep applying paint here and there to get a good coating. Overall, they're nice for hobbyists and crafters, but may not be up to professional standards. They come in a securely sewn storage pack that has a smoothly functioning zipper. The set doesn't have names or numbers for the individual pens, so it could get confusing trying to remember which shade you are supposed to be using. It would be much better if they were numbered, but it's a nice set and I recommend it for amateur artists, crafters, and as a much cleaner alternative to traditional paint and brush setups.

Content: I have had a need for acrylic markers.  Everyone in the family has different things they are doing, but I prefer we all have our own sets to use.  I got this one for our son who wanted a complete set for his 3D gaming projects which are extensive and intricate.BOXThe box with this set is GREAT.  It is a not hard to get the markers out, but they are not in order which makes doing the swatch sheet annoying and frustrating.  If you want to make the sheet easier to access markers from, you will need to put them in order yourself.SWATCH SHEETThankfully this comes with a really nice heavy duty paper swatch sheet.  It allows for really good swatches to be made for reference.MARKERSThe markers do not have color names, but each cap is marked with the color number.  There is a window in the side which allows you to see if the paint needs mixing, or if the levels are getting too low.  You can shake each one easily side to side, just don't go nuts with it.LEAKAGE?There was no leakage with these markers.  Flow was even and nice for almost all colors.COLORSThis is the most complete set of colors I have ever seen.  It is really nice and covers any type of project you can imagine.TIPSThere is a bag of replacement tips if you need one.PERFORMANCEThe performmance of these markers is really nice.  The colors are pretty decent, the application is smooth, and it allows for fine details or broader coverage.  I like these on paper and canvas a lot.  I am not as fond of them on glass or smooth plastic.  They tend to chip or scratch off if hit just right.ONE ISSUEI had no colors missing, but one of the colors has the tip put in backwards.  I haven't had the opportunity to change it around yet.THE BOTTOM LINEThis box is great, the swatch sheet is great, and the markers/pens are good performers.MY RATINGFIVE STARS.  This set of markers is a great collection.  None of th pens were dry, all of them worked well, and with the exception of the upside down tip they performed very well.  I highly suggest these, ,but use testing before doing a project to see how well it lasts on the surface you intend to use.DOES HE LIKE ITOur son really loves this set.  He is already opening up his 3D gaming manufacturing for his projects and enjyoing the flexibility that it allows for his textured plastic pieces and landscaping set ups.

Content: I love the variety of colors this set of brush acrylic markers offers. I've been using paint pens or acrylic markers for about 7 or 8 years. But I have another statue to paint and several signs to repaint that have been sun bleached over the years. So I will update if I need to on how they last outdoors. I have submitted a small cartoon that I sketched & painted just for this review, with the number markers provided. Just to show you how true the colors are. I am very pleased and excited to continue on my paint marker journey. And can I just say for the record paint markers are the best thing since sliced bread. They have changed the game. Well done thank you!

Content: This is a beautiful set of paint markers. My daughter's and I have been using them every day since they arrived. All 3 of us took turns doing the swatches. Which was actually really fun - and a bit stressful at times.The numbering system of these paint markers is an absolute atrocity lol. I didn't remove any stars for the numbering because the markers themselves are great.The colors are numbered - from 600's - 900's. 6 and 9 are the two worst possible numbers you can use for a numbering tangible items. It's so easy to conflate one for the other. Some of these pens caps had little dots on them (either above or below the 6 or 9?!) since no one knows if the dot indicates up or down/top or bottom, it's essentially just a useless decorative mark above or below a 6 or a 9 lol.About halfway into the color chart, I started to see a pattern and deduced that the colors seem to be more organized by their secondary tones/color temperatures as opposed to primary. I also realized that most are grouped into similar colors, so you can look in the same color family as the previous one for the next number. However, when a new undertone section starts, you won't know - and good luck finding the numbered pen you're looking for at that point haha.Aside from the numbering nightmare lol, these are perfect. Every single one worked flawlessly and had a great flow. The colors are vivid and there is pretty much every color you can think of. I did notice that a few tips were more flexible than others. I definitely prefer the firmer ones are they are easier to control for smaller designs - which is mostly what I do.  This set also includes extra tips - which is appreciated.If your planning to buy this set of 240 paint pens, keep an eye on the price. When I acquired this, it was selling for close to $150. At the time of this review, it's selling for $118. If you break it down, it's like 50¢ per marker. Which is pretty reasonable compared to Posca. I think this set would make an awesome gift for anyone who loves art. My teenage daughter's and I have been painting rocks with these and they work beautifully for it. But there are so many applications for these besides just rocks. We are very happy with them and although the color swatching was a bit maddening, I really did enjoy the challenge of it.

Content: I would definitely see this as an investment at this price, I feel it's a really good price for what you're getting. There are 240 acrylic markers in the set, so be prepared to spend some time getting them in order, because they do NOT come that way. Also, the numbers do not make any sense at all! There are some hundreds apart and then you'll come across the rare gem with a few in order (very few!)... But a treat when you're sorting this many. But it would be nice if these numbers meant anything at all versus the randomness that exists. I got over that annoyance, at least a little, by the fact that the lids are a very close match, if not exact, to the color you'll get on the swatch card. That's refreshing! There were only a few things I found during my long swatching and reorganizing session and those were as follows: 1) I found a weird black substance on one of the pens and later on the paper when one of the pieces fell off. No idea what it is, but it's pictured, 2) there was a visible "division" or splitting of the paint in the window of one of my markers. I don't know if it matters or if it's all mixed up in the end when you shake the pen each time?, 3) I had the felt from the end come off a few times while marking in the little swatch box. I can only imagine what this would do on a rough or large surface!! On one it came off in little pieces and ended up in/under the paint causing it to be all bumpy (see arrows in pic). The other few times it happened it was all one piece and while it did dull the tip slightly, it wasn't a huge enough chunk to make a big difference., and 4) the annoyance that this large set of 240 markers didn't come with a better divided box. It has thin dividers that are barely held in place by a notch and mine is broken. I don't know if it was already like that, but I don't know of it happening that I was aware of. It just makes it even harder to keep the pens in place while trying to sort them. And because they don't have they're own individual spot (or at min. their own rows) they move around every time you take one out, therefore causing a bit of an ordeal **everytime** you remove a marker and go to put it back in. This would've been eliminated had these been in a case where each marker has it's own spot. I don't need a headache each time I use these and I can see this making me not want to deal with them and choosing one of my other sets instead. Overall I think it's a good buy, but with 240 chances for something to go wrong, I only had a handful, so that's good. I felt it was worth about 3.5 stars sure to the issues (the biggest deduction because of the box not being properly divided bc it is a huge hassle) but since I can't do that, I gave 4.I tried to be as thorough as possible and include pictures so you could see for yourself what you'll receive (or potentially in the case of issues... Hopefully those are left out of your order!;)) But I hope you found it helpful. Take care and happy creating & painting!

Content:
Definitely get these if you want an high-quality beginner’s set of acrylic markers…you just can’t beat this price for the quality and variety of markers you receive!!

**IT IS VERY IMPORTANT that you STORE THESE MARKERS ON THEIR SIDES AND FLIP THE CASE OVER EVERY WEEK OR SO** this tip is for ANY art markers. Streaking or bleeding can be caused by the ink or paint settling on one side or the other. Particularly if these have been stored vertically in the warehouse. For dual end markers, always store the case so that the markers lay on their side, and the flip the case on its other side anytime you think about it.

Do some test swatches and practice drawings before starting on your final project. This way you understand how these particular markers perform. If you’d re having a problem with streaking, lay the case on its side overnight, and also flip the case to the other side for the next morning, then try again. Usually solves the problem with new markers!

Yes, the individual markers *don’t* come labeled with numbers or color names, BUT they come with a chart to assist and have colored caps at both ends. When you think of how many countries (with different languages) they have to ship these to, I think this plan makes sense.

Don’t mix up the caps! But it’s also a good reminder to instantly replace the caps after you use a specific marker….you DON’T want to leave the caps off of acrylic markers longer than you have to in order to color with them.

Also consider the cost savings of not labeling each individual marker….savings that got passed on to us!

I’m impressed with the case quality. I received a different case of markers from another brand, and that case was very flimsy—not this case!!

This is a great deal for good quality markers. 5/5

Content:
For what I like, I would have probably given 3 stars, but I want to review these paint markers for what they are. Personally the paint inside isn’t up to my standards, but considering the price and the amount of markers, in addition to a case, they’re what I expected.

First, they come in a zippered case which I prefer over a cardboard box, which I wish more companies would do. Each marker has its own slot and the inserts are removable. It also comes with a printed swatch chart and extra nibs. Some of the swatches are pretty close, some are not, so you’ll want to make your own. The chart has names and numbers, but there’s no markings on the paint pens themselves - kinda pointless and you have to just go by the cap color. As long as you have a chart and keep them in order I guess it’s not that bad, but what if you take multiple out or use different storage? When swatching them, I noticed that some are nice and “juicy” where the paint flows nicely, but others are dryer, and you’ll need to go slower to get better coverage. The paint is on the thinner side, so they can get a little streaky, and the opacity just isn’t there. The dark colors are obviously better, but mid tones (like red) didn’t cover black ink, even with three coats, and some of the dark colors (like dark green) failed here, too. Personally, I prefer opaque paint, but this might not be a negative for some. Of the colors, I do think there’s a nice selection of warm, cool, a couple of skin tone, and neutral colors, and even a handful of metallic. For a beginner set, I think there’s colors are good to get started for sure.

I plan to play around with them a little more, but I think this set will get passed along to the kids for their projects and play. For the current price, they’re worth checking out, and would make a good gift for kids. If you are familiar with some of the more expensive brands of paint markers though, I would probably skip these. It just depends on what you want them for.

Content:
I have had this set for 20 days and it has pulled its weight on a bunch of projects. First stroke out of the cap was clean with no shaking or priming. The brush tips feel springy and make thin outlines or solid fills without fighting me. Coverage is strong. On paper and canvas I get crisp lines in 1 coat. On plastic and a dark river rock I needed 2 quick coats, and the second went on soon after the first without lifting the color.

I tested a handful of surfaces. Cardstock, canvas panel, a 3D print, a glazed mug, and a few garden stones. The ink flow stayed even and I did not see sputtering. On glass labels the writing stayed put through dry wiping and light scratches. It lifted with a wet paper towel, which is actually handy for temporary kitchen labels. Once fully dry on the rocks and mug it held up to a rinse in cool water.

The color range is generous. Most hues pop and layer well. A few shades are very close, so I filled in the swatch card and put tiny dots on the caps to speed up picking the right one. Dry time depends on the surface. Paper was touch safe in about 2 min. Smooth plastic was closer to 5. The see through ink window is useful, and the divided storage box keeps everything tidy in a backpack. Extra tips are a smart bonus.

For the size of the set and how reliably these write, the value feels excellent. Easy start, bright results, and dependable control across materials. I reach for them now when I want paint look with marker speed.

Content:
I’m absolutely in love with these markers! I recently had the chance to use them for some artwork (I'll be sharing pictures soon), and they completely exceeded my expectations in every way. From the moment I opened the set, I was impressed with the vibrant color selection. With 80 shades to choose from, there’s a perfect hue for any project, whether you're looking for something bold and eye-catching or soft and subtle. Additionally, the dual-tipped design provides incredible versatility, enabling you to work with greater precision on fine details or cover larger areas with ease, depending on the project or surface you’re working on.

The paint itself flows beautifully—smooth and consistent. I’ve worked with other paint markers before, but these have an especially nice texture. The colors layer effortlessly on top of one another, giving you the ability to create depth and dimension in your artwork. I've used these on a variety of surfaces, including canvas, rocks, wood, and even fabric, and the results have been consistently fantastic. The markers perform well on each material, with no bleeding or fading, and the color payoff is rich and true to the cap’s shade.

The quality of the markers feels top-notch, which is something I really appreciate. They have a premium, well-constructed feel, and yet they’re surprisingly beginner-friendly. You don’t need to be a professional artist to get good results with these, but even as someone who has experience with more advanced projects, I found them incredibly fun and easy to use. Most of the colors have great opacity, even on darker surfaces, and the blending ability is better than I anticipated, especially for acrylic markers. It’s easy to mix and layer colors without them becoming muddy or streaky, which makes a huge difference when you’re trying to achieve smooth transitions or soft gradients in your art.

Another thing I really love is how well the tips hold their shape. I’ve had markers in the past where the tips lose their form after only a few uses, but these maintain their point for precision and offer smooth, even coverage every time. I’ve also noticed no issues with drying out or skipping, which can be a problem with cheaper markers. I’ve been able to work for extended periods without needing to shake or prime the pens, which is a huge plus when you’re in the zone.

Now, I do have a tiny complaint, but it’s really nothing major. A few of the darker colors, especially the deep reds and blacks, can bleed a little when you’re using them on thinner paper. However, this is pretty common with highly pigmented acrylic markers, so it wasn’t a dealbreaker for me. It’s just something to keep in mind if you plan on using them for detailed line work on thin paper—especially if you're working with delicate materials or want to avoid any bleed-through.

All in all, I’m beyond pleased with these markers, and I’m giving them a solid 5 stars. They’ve been a fantastic addition to my art supplies, and I know I’ll be reaching for them again and again in the future. Whether you’re a beginner looking to try out paint markers for the first time or an experienced artist searching for a new tool to elevate your work, these markers are an amazing choice. Content:
I ordered these markers for the purpose of decorating smooth rocks. I am not a crafty person so I don't know if I am supposed to prime/seal/coat/etc a surface like a rock before painting it, so I didn't. I just drew directly on the rocks.

The  rocks were about 2" in diameter. I found the fine tip end to be good for more precision drawing or for writing. The blunt tip end was good for coloring in designs and whatnot.

My rocks were a light tannish-grey color. I colored one completely white so I could draw on a white surface. 1 basic layer had pretty good coverage, but you could still see the darker tint of the rock beneath. 2 thick layers was much better, almost completely opaque. I probably could have gone a little lighter handed, but while the blunt tip is good for general use I feel like I needed a wider tip to color the entire rock evenly. You can faintly see marker lines. If  I was coloring a smaller rock it probably would be quick and thorough work.

I found that in general I needed more than 1 coat of the paint coloring over the rocks described above. 1 coat of paint goes on rich and bold, but as it dries it fades. I can see how precisely adding additional coats could be difficult for tasks such as writing or fine lines. I'm guessing this is due to the paint seeping into any micro cracks and holes in the rock surface, so in hindsight priming the rock first is probably the way to go to save yourself from using a lot of paint, as well as coloring over lighter surfaces.

I am glad I ordered them for my project and am satisfied with the turn out. I also appreciate the convenience and lack of mess that can accompany traditional painting.

Content: After completing a single project, it will become second nature to grip the correct side of the barrel since it specifies both tip sizes on each barrel: 1 mm fine on one end and 1-5 mm dot on the other. It just took a few fast shakes and a little squeeze for the color to flow evenly on the very first attempt. The fine nib had a structure that was rigid enough to produce letter-weight lines on paper, but it was also flexible enough to glide over the uneven surface of river rock. By switching to the dot tip, I was able to create smooth circles that could be broadened or narrowed depending only on the amount of pressure used, which eliminated the need for me to search for toothpicks and ball tools. A real carbon black, delicate pastels, shiny gold, and sharp primaries are all included in the palette this time around. On a canvas panel that had been primed, the colors dried to a satin finish that was uniform throughout, with no patchiness or edge bloom. It was shown that the binder is able to adhere to surfaces rather than float on them by the fact that metallics maintained their shimmer on both polished glass and porous terracotta. Two coats were required to obtain full opacity on slate coasters; yet, after a single pass, the fabric absorbed just enough to provide the look of a vintage wash. This adaptability was something I did not anticipate from a single ink formulation.

Content:
Since I enjoy all kinds of crafts and have crafty kids, I was excited to try this set of acrylic markers from Artecho. To summarize, I think it is a decent value for mixed-media use, especially for use with kids. However, a lack of quality control and many similar colors may not satisfy an adult artist.

Pros: I have used many types of non-toxic and paint markers in the past on a variety of mediums, and was thrilled to receive 72 colors in this set. The brush heads are smooth and a delight to work with. The fine tips most resemble traditional press-down paint marker tips, though you don't have to press these down to work - a real improvement! The rainbow of colors is very attractive in the protective, easy-to-transport case. All markers can be easily accessed when the case is open.

Now for the drawbacks. Some of the paints look best on shiny surfaces, but tend to rub off when touched, even after drying. Once fully dried, the acrylic has the best staying-power on matte surfaces without using a fixative. Some of the colors are really beautiful and smooth ("carmine", "sapphire"). Others are weakly pigmented or look muddy ("watermelon", "emerald"). The weak pigments don’t cover darker surfaces or lines, so beware if you’re trying to layer. I was super disappointed at the noticeable difference between the color of the brush and fine tip on many of the markers. See the picture of the color chart: the upper half of each box is the brush side, and the lower half of the box is the fine tip. In most cases, the brush color was quite a bit more pigmented and vibrant than the fine tip color. This difference means I cannot switch between tip types and expect my work to look consistent.

The numbering system and color names seem illogical, and the markers are not organized in the case according to either the numbering or the color chart. Many of the names inadequately reflect the actual color; for example, "brown" is a light pink, and "indigo" is a greenish gray. "Blackberry" and "crimson" are both pale pink. In fact, 18 of the markers are pink tones, including "beige", "camel", and "earth red", and similar in appearance. As the paints are not true to the color of their lids, it is hard to find particular shades unless you rearrange them and use a color chart. However, the included chart lists 120 colors, and there are only 72 in this set, leaving many blank boxes. The color chart is also printed on shiny paper, so the colors tend to smear.

Overall, I think the value of this introductory set is fine at its current price point (24 u.s.d. at the time of review). The markers will be good for painting on stones, wood, and other mixed media crafts with kids (especially kids who like pink), and I think they'll hold up through multiple projects. However, if you're a serious artist or looking to add to your existing stock of acrylic markers, I don't recommend this set from Artecho.

Content:
I have been using old-school, strong-smelling, quick-to-dry-out paint pens for many years, but when I saw these WUO acrylic paint markers that didn’t require pressing and holding, I had to try them. What I wasn’t expecting was how much better they would be.

* Color Range & Appearance: I went with the 60-color set, and I’m glad I did. The colors cover a nice spectrum, including a few pale shades that don’t look obvious from the pen exteriors. For example, the pens made me think there was no pale green, but once tested, there were actually a couple of lighter greens. I’d still love to see extra black, white, gold, and silver included, since those get used up quickly.

* Application & Coverage: The paint goes on somewhat thin (not thick and globby), which turns out to be a strength. It allows layering and blending instead of clumping or streaking. On paper, the coverage is smooth and much nicer than regular markers. On ceramics, you’ll likely need more than one coat like I did. They also work over other acrylic paints (a little tougher on ones that dry glossy, I found), but I find they perform best directly on unfinished ceramic surfaces.

* Packaging & Storage: The set comes in stackable plastic trays that look neat and high-end. Each tray snaps securely into the one below it: tilt the back down first, then lower the front, and finally lock it with the white toggle on the front. I really like this design for keeping them organized.

* Extras: There are tester cards so you can preview how each color looks on black and white paper, plus some small project ideas. One even involves painting onto a sponge, adding water, and watching it puff up, which was fun.

* Odor & Safety: Unlike traditional paint pens, these have no odor at all, which surprised me. That makes them much more pleasant to use and safe for children, though you’d still want to be careful about clothing and surfaces.

* Use Case: I definitely plan to use these for craft projects, but I'm thinking that I'll also use them for detail work on larger acrylic canvas paintings that I do. They shake easily to refresh the paint flow when needed, and I haven’t had issues with clogging. Just avoid pressing too hard on the tips since that could damage them.

* Wishlist for Improvement:
⦁ Pen exterior colors don’t always match the actual paint shade.
⦁ Include more duplicate “workhorse” colors (black, white, gold, silver).
⦁ Offer a fine liner option (about half the tip width) for super-detailed work.

* Value for the Cost: At 39.99 at the time I'm writing this, that's not cheap for a set of craft pens. But, this is a really large set and if  you were to buy each pen individually you would pay much more. Plus you're getting craft projects to go with it. So, all in all, I think this is an exceptional value for the cost...which I hope doesn't change.

* Bottom Line: These paint pens exceeded my expectations. The colors are vibrant, the pens layer and blend well, they store easily, and best of all, they’re odor-free. They make me want to reach for them instead of my old paint pens. Super highly recommended. Go for the kit of 60 if you regularly do crafts and/or use acrylic paints.

Content: This TECADA 168 Colors Acrylic Paint Brush Markers is a weird mix of really good and really not good. I am a professional artist, and I own thousands of acrylic markers, to be able to compare to. The first red flag I see is that the name is Tecada, but the item I received is called Flysea markers. They use the exact same box as a ton of other Chinese paint markers, and the same random extremely unhelpful number system. I was quite worried this would just be a duplicate of other sets I have.The next red flag is that these markers are brand new, but already the numbers - the literal only way to distinguish each marker from each other - are half wiped off. That has already rendered some of them virtually impossible to use.I was fortunate to receive all the markers in the box, and for the most part they are all distinct colors. The box is not good though - competing brands include a zip case organizer with elastic strap loops, and that is far more worth one's money, to be able to keep these in the color order you need them - but good luck taking the time to re-sort all 168 by color order. Moreover, the color swatch on the bottom of the box, is not covered by anything, so all the swatches (this not being real acrylic which is plastic, but some cheap craft gouache) have mostly scraped off within a week from just gently moving the box around.Some of these are actually very decently pigmented, more than other brands, which was a pleasant shock. Most have low opacity though, and you'll be using a lot of layers for a long time spent, if you actually want to color over anything completely. This is more of a layering marker. I was also pleased that generally speaking, these are not an exact match to my other sets - even those with essentially the same box and unmarked markers. They do NOT say Guangna, which is great, because nearly all of this type when you buy them under whatever random name, what you receive is a marker that says GuangNa on the side, and those are both very translucent, and also often very repetitive. These are no-name.Another major good point was that these are as waterproof as POSCA or other similar markers... which is to say, mostly. They, like those, can have a slight bleed with certain colors, or other paints.The best part of this set is that the color swatches are arranged by color, even though the numbers make no sense. That is the one thing that makes this the most usable.The color range is decent, with a few actual dark colors, and a few more realistic greens than most have. This set does not have any actual dark brown - only very chalky browns - and it does not have enough reds. There is not 1 single actual orange in the whole set. Don't buy this looking for orange.Overall, this is a hit and miss set, that for what it offers seems way overpriced to me. When ordered, it was a whopping $77. But I personally would not pay more than maybe $45, given the tons of competing markers on the market. But this really all depends on what you are expecting to do with this. If you need it to be opaque, look elsewhere. If you want layering, and a new range of colors, with some actual darks, this may be a good addition to your collection. I really liked some of the unusual colors provided, that are unlike those in other sets - some more complex grays, a deep red and green, a decent yellow range.For me personally, I would never recommend buying this to anyone, until they fix the markers so the number labeling actually STAYS on the marker. They, and all the time you spent coloring in the swatches - are absolutely useless if you cannot identify any of the markers. If not, that would transform this to a set only useful for 6 year olds. And who is going to spend $77 on a set of markers for 6 year olds? Not me. That price is for people who are actually serious about their coloring, and who are at the least serious crafters, if not semi-pro artists.This set is very low quality, mixed with some random high quality elements, and some well-pigmented colors.

Content:
I craft handmade art greetings cards for my friends rather than buy commercial ones. There have been times that I need metallic ink to sign or title my card art. Unfortunately, metallic gel pens clogs easily and also scratches the paper because I need to apply more pressure to get the ink to flow. Marker inks are iffy about bleeding through paper card stock.

Prudiut's 12 Pack Metallic Markers handles card stock art paper well. It dries so fast that there is no bleed through using the brush tip for coloring. The paint remains on the top of the paper. Because the marker paint dries really fast, by the time I grab and open another pen color, the previous paint is dry enough to add dots and details. No smudges on my hands or on the art because the paint dries so quickly.

The pens feels more like painting than drawing. The metallic paint markers flow smoothly like brushed on paint. I am also going to use the metallic markers to highlight and sign my acrylic paintings on canvas. I think the metallic markers would be excellent on adding make-up effects on my handmade ceramic dolls.

The only mess I had with the markers is when taking the caps off. The caps are so stuck on to the pens, that it takes a bit of force to pull off which results in me accidentally getting paint on the fingers that are pulling the cap off. The paint does not rub off when it dries on my skin but it does wash off easy with hand soap and water.

Overall, I am very pleased with the performance and color of Prudiut's 12 Pack Metallic Markers.

Content:
This set of acrylic markers has exceeded my expectations. They are easy to use (no priming, no shaking, just uncap and get to creating!), and they write beautifully. They would be awesome for general painting applications on pretty much any surface but would also function very nicely for hand lettering.
They dry quickly - but not instantly, so be careful not to smudge them. Wait a few seconds, though and after that they stay put.
The color range of these markers is really interesting. They're all vibrant and well-pigmented, and there is a range of both standard bright shades, a few fluorescents, and even a really nice range of Morandi-style muted tones that are just gorgeous. There are also a gold and silver metallic that shine so nicely!
They generally provide good coverage, though some of the paler shades are a lot more translucent than I'd like (but it seems that's a problem across almost every brand, save a few. I put down some black and then tried the white over the top and it was not opaque at all. Aside from maybe 4 or 5 of the palest shades though, most of these markers will likely work well on black paper and other darker surfaces.
The brush tips are very nice. They're not all exactly consistent in firmness or in juiciness, but none of them were dry and all of them are quite functional (just some are juicier than others).
I'm concerned a bit about how long these will last since each pen contains two different colors, so the capacity for each color may be less than you would find in a single-color pen, but time will tell!
I look forward to trying their single-color acrylic markers soon, too. These rival most of the other brands that I own, and I can't say enough good things about not having to prime and shake before use.

Content:
I have the smaller 36 pack of dual Grabie markers, so when I saw they had come out with a larger pack, I grabbed them up.:)

They are the same size and quality as the smaller pack, although the coloring on the marker packaging is different (relief). They also seem to have gone through a color name and number change for some of the colors that were included in the 36; you'll find most of the 36 pack here (with some that look slightly different). This pack covers a wide variety of colors, and there weren't really any (for this coloring anyways) that I was wishing were included.

I absolutely love that these don't have to be primed, and they have brush tips instead of hard nibs. The downside is that if you aren't careful (and honestly, even if you are), the tips of the brushes can break down farely quickly, which makes more detailed work very hard. They can also get bits of dried paint on them, so be prepared to pick the little bits off.
As of writing this, I don't think Grabie offers replacement tips, but I believe they are pretty similar to another brands brush tips, that you can buy replacements for, fairly cheap.

The really lovely thing about these is that they don't bleed through (like some acrylics have separation liquid that leaks through). You can easily color a double sided page, and have zero issues come through the back (given your paper quality, super thin types might show through, I'm unsure).

There's mutliple ways to use these; on rocks, glass paper, vinyl, plastic, etc (given you have a sealant) and I'm still finding extra uses for them, like adding details to coloring pages, or fixing some art when I've gone outside the lines with the medium I'm using, or even to bring back the original color on clay that's darkened too much.

They're very opaque, so you do need to be careful when coloring in pages; you'll want to have a fineliner ready to go over lines if you color over, as these will either soften the lines, or completely wipe them out. You need to be slow while coloring portions in, because if you are fast, you'll get streaks or blotches in the paint (like some areas of my coloring page; book is A Million Kittens). Do make sure to shake them prior to using to blend them.

My main gripe is that they really downgraded on the carry case packaging. I love the 36 pack case; it's softer plastic and textured, with no sharp edges, and it's easy to pull the markers out (and put them back).
With this larger pack, the packaging is a thicker, cheaper plastic that I can't get the markers out, or put them away, without scraping my hands up from the sharp opening. It can be frustrating. I really wish they'd stayed with the same packaging.

I do really like these and they've gone into my travel art bag. My original pack has yet to run out of ink, so they seem like they last a good bit. I'll have to report back if/when they do.
